title: Funneling And Sculpting Of Optical Waves Through Non-Magnetic Metasurfaces
authors: Nooshin M. Estakhri Nasim Mohammadi Estakhri
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient concentration and transport of electromagnetic energy through electromagnetically thick structures often requires resonant phenomenon and careful design considerations. Here, we introduce a realistic non-resonant approach based on electromagnetically thick self-dual metasurfaces that can funnel electromagnetic waves through subwavelength regions and without requiring magnetic materials. By satisfying the self-duality condition, the proposed metasurfaces support impedance-matched propagation and enable reflectionless energy transfer regardless of the metasurface thickness or structural details. This mechanism also allows selected control over the internal field while maintaining reasonable operational bandwidth. Metasurface elements are designed individually, and full-wave simulations confirm the predicted behavior in sample representative cases. The proposed framework provides a general strategy for robust electromagnetic energy routing and confinement, with potential impact in nonlinear optics, sensing and particle manipulation, near-field imaging, advanced absorber technologies, and wide-angle antenna systems.
tldr: This paper presents a non-resonant approach using self-dual metasurfaces to funnel and sculpt electromagnetic waves through subwavelength regions without magnetic materials.
motivation: Efficient concentration and transport of electromagnetic energy through thick structures typically require resonant phenomena and careful design. The authors aim to achieve this with a non-magnetic, non-resonant metasurface approach.
method: The method involves designing electromagnetically thick self-dual metasurfaces that satisfy the self-duality condition, enabling impedance-matched propagation and reflectionless energy transfer. Full-wave simulations validate the design.
result: The proposed metasurfaces support reflectionless energy transfer regardless of thickness or structural details, and allow selective control over internal fields with reasonable bandwidth.
conclusion: The framework provides a general strategy for robust electromagnetic energy routing and confinement, with potential applications in nonlinear optics, sensing, particle manipulation, near-field imaging, absorbers, and antenna systems.

title: Constraints On Yukawa-type New Forces From The Lamb Shift In Muonic Hydrogen And Deuterium
authors: Li-Bang Wang Chung-Chien Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an analytical framework to constrain Yukawa-type fifth-force interactions using the Lamb shift in hydrogen and deuterium. The sixfold coordinate-space integral for the energy shift is transformed into a one-dimensional momentum-space convolution of the atomic form factor and the Yukawa potential, eliminating the need for approximations. This formulation directly incorporates empirical nuclear charge distributions through their form factors, making the implementation of experimental results straightforward. Applying this method to the latest hydrogen and deuterium spectroscopy data, we derive constraints on the coupling constant [MATH] in the interaction range [MATH]~fm. A resonance-like cancellation between the [MATH] and [MATH] orbital shifts is identified at a critical range [MATH]~fm, where the energy shift vanishes and the constraint on [MATH] diverges, marking a transition between attractive and repulsive regimes. The constraints are shown to be independent of the nuclear charge distribution model. Our results indicate that the transition frequency shifts induced by such new forces lie well below current spectroscopic resolution, establishing spectroscopic precision as the primary bottleneck for probing these interactions.
tldr: This paper constrains Yukawa-type fifth forces using Lamb shift measurements in muonic hydrogen and deuterium.
motivation: To search for new physics beyond the Standard Model by probing hypothetical fifth forces at sub-nuclear scales.
method: Develops an analytical framework transforming the sixfold coordinate-space integral into a one-dimensional momentum-space convolution of atomic form factor and Yukawa potential.
result: Derives constraints on the coupling constant over interaction ranges ~fm, identifying a resonance-like cancellation at a critical range where the energy shift vanishes.
conclusion: The induced transition frequency shifts are below current spectroscopic resolution, so improved precision is needed to detect such forces.

title: Refractive-index Tomography Of Opaque Tissue From Its Own Backscattered Light
authors: Tran Dinh Hoang, Jaecheol Cho, Thi van Anh Nguyen, Eunyoung Seong, Joowon Lim, Jin Hee Hong, Yongwoo Kwon, Jun Wan Kim, Juhee Yang, Seokchan Yoon, Sungsam Kang, Wonshik Choi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The refractive index (RI) is an intrinsic, label-free marker of a living cell's dry mass and subcellular morphology, and hence of its physiological state. Its three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction has become a powerful way to study cells and tissues in their native state, spanning cell growth, drug response and disease diagnosis. Yet this capability rests on a fundamental constraint: the RI can be recovered only from light transmitted through the specimen, which demands optical access to both sides. The cells that matter most -- those within thick tissues, intact organs and living animals -- are therefore out of reach. A tissue, however, can illuminate its own cells from behind: light backscattered by intrinsic tissue structures beneath a cell carries the same transmission information a microscope would collect from the far side. Here we develop a divide-and-conquer inverse-scattering framework that recovers this transmission from the backscattering and reconstructs a cell's 3D RI. We demonstrate label-free, quantitative imaging of cells within an engineered tissue, and a living mouse through its intact skull, where we further quantify the dry mass of individual osteocytes in vivo. By removing the need for two-sided access, this reflection-only approach extends RI tomography into living tissue, enabling non-destructive, longitudinal imaging of cells in their native environment.
tldr: This paper presents a method for 3D refractive index tomography of cells within opaque tissue using only backscattered light, enabling label-free imaging in vivo.
motivation: Current refractive index tomography requires transmitted light, limiting its application to thin samples; the authors aim to extend it to thick tissues and living animals.
method: A divide-and-conquer inverse-scattering framework recovers transmission information from backscattered light, reconstructing the 3D refractive index of cells.
result: Demonstrated label-free imaging of cells in engineered tissue and through the intact skull of a living mouse, quantifying dry mass of individual osteocytes in vivo.
conclusion: This reflection-only approach removes the need for two-sided optical access, enabling non-destructive longitudinal imaging of cells in their native environment.

title: Engineering Disordered Many-particle Plasmonic Nanoclusters For Wafer-scale Uniform And Giant Electromagnetic Field Enhancement
authors: Minjun Kim, Vasanthan Devaraj, Hyeon-Seok Seo, Seongjae Eom, Jeong-Su Lee, Donghan Lee, Min Yong Jeon, Thomas Zentgraf, Jong-Min Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalable plasmonic technologies face a critical trade-off: few-body architectures offer high enhancement but are sensitive to fabrication flaws, while scalable methods like solid-state dewetting yield large, low-enhancement gaps. We introduce a paradigm shift using a many-body plasmonic architecture inspired by statistical mechanics. By moving toward the continuum limit (N>>1), local geometric variations are statistically averaged out, effectively decoupling optical performance from microscopic disorder. We implement this concept via a lithography- and etching-free, multi-step dewetting strategy, creating wafer-scale nanoclusters. This process strategically forms a robust many-body system by introducing numerous small satellite nanoparticles between larger particles. Crucially, this design achieves a high collective enhancement that surpasses even optimized few-body systems, despite having larger individual gaps. Under optimized conditions, these substrates exhibit a surface-enhanced Raman scattering enhancement factor approaching 4 x 108 with unprecedented reproducibility (RSD of ~10%). This scalable, low-cost concept establishes a practical route toward reproducible wafer-scale nanophotonic platforms for sensing, spectroscopy, and quantum technologies.
tldr: This paper presents a scalable method to fabricate plasmonic nanoclusters with high and uniform electromagnetic field enhancement for sensing and spectroscopy.
motivation: Scalable plasmonic technologies suffer from a trade-off between high enhancement and fabrication robustness; the authors aim to overcome this using a many-body architecture.
method: A lithography- and etching-free multi-step dewetting strategy creates wafer-scale nanoclusters with many satellite nanoparticles, statistically averaging out local geometric variations.
result: The substrates achieve a surface-enhanced Raman scattering enhancement factor of ~4×10^8 with ~10% relative standard deviation, surpassing optimized few-body systems.
conclusion: This low-cost, scalable approach provides reproducible wafer-scale nanophotonic platforms for sensing, spectroscopy, and quantum technologies.

title: Measures Of Maximal Entropy For Markovian Dynamics On The Gehman Dendrite
authors: Jakub Tomaszewski Piotr Oprocha
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study transitive dynamical systems on the Gehman dendrite [MATH] for which the endpoint set [MATH] is invariant. Our goal is to approximate such systems by maps whose measure-theoretic behaviour at maximal entropy is governed by an explicit countable Markov structure. We introduce a class of Markovian maps, encode their dynamics by countable Markov graphs, and use the criteria of Vere-Jones, Gurevich, Salama and Ruette to control the existence of measures of maximal entropy. The main theorem gives two arbitrarily close mixing Markovian perturbations of any given system in the considered class: one has a unique measure of maximal entropy, while the other has none.
tldr: This paper studies measures of maximal entropy for Markovian dynamics on the Gehman dendrite, a topological space, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to approximate transitive dynamical systems on the Gehman dendrite by Markovian maps and analyze the existence of measures of maximal entropy.
method: They introduce a class of Markovian maps, encode dynamics via countable Markov graphs, and apply criteria from Vere-Jones, Gurevich, Salama, and Ruette to control existence of maximal entropy measures.
result: The main theorem provides two arbitrarily close mixing Markovian perturbations: one with a unique measure of maximal entropy, the other with none.
conclusion: The work contributes to topological dynamics and ergodic theory, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sphere Constraints And Harmonic Map Flow: Controllability And Reachability By Low-Mode Forcing
authors: Debopriya Mukherjee, Kistosil Fahim, Erika Hausenblas
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the controllability and reachability of sphere-constrained evolution equations under degenerate (low-mode) forcing, with the harmonic map heat flow as the principal application. Exploiting the underlying geometric structure, we reformulate the problem as an infinite-dimensional control-affine system in Fourier variables and analyze the Lie algebra generated by the controlled vector fields. We prove that iterated Lie brackets generate new admissible directions, providing a mechanism through which finitely many control modes propagate their influence across infinitely many Fourier components. The results provide a Lie-algebraic framework for controlling manifold-valued evolution equations.
tldr: This paper studies controllability of sphere-constrained evolution equations using low-mode forcing, with harmonic map heat flow as an application.
motivation: To understand how finitely many control modes can influence infinite-dimensional systems constrained to a sphere, which is a fundamental problem in control theory.
method: The problem is reformulated as an infinite-dimensional control-affine system in Fourier variables, and the Lie algebra generated by controlled vector fields is analyzed.
result: Iterated Lie brackets generate new admissible directions, showing that finitely many control modes can propagate influence across infinitely many Fourier components.
conclusion: The work provides a Lie-algebraic framework for controlling manifold-valued evolution equations, but it is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Boson-fermion Meromorphic Open-string Vertex Algebras And Their Canonically Twisted Modules
authors: Qixuan Fang, Yi-Zhi Huang, Fei Qi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a [MATH]-graded meromorphic open-string vertex algebra from a finite-dimensional vector space with a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form, together with its canonically twisted module. This algebra is generated by suitable noncommutative generalizations of bosonic and fermionic fields and is a noncommutative generalization of the free boson-fermion vertex operator superalgebra. Similarly to the purely bosonic and purely fermionic cases in the early works by the second author in [H1], by Fiordalisi and the third author in [FQ], and by the third author in [Q3], the usual super-commutatitive relations between creation and annihilation operators still hold while no relations exist among creation operators. In particular, normal-ordering remains well-defined. As in [H1], [FQ], and [Q3], we prove a generalized Wick's theorem in this case, which gives a formula for a product of two normal ordered products of bosonic and fermionic generating fields. Using this generalized Wick's theorem, we construct the [MATH]-graded meromorphic open-string vertex algebra and its canonically twisted module in this case. The construction in this paper is the algebraic part of our construction of suitable Dirac-like operators from spin manifolds.
tldr: This paper constructs a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra from bosonic and fermionic fields, generalizing free boson-fermion vertex operator superalgebras.
motivation: The authors aim to develop algebraic structures needed for constructing Dirac-like operators from spin manifolds, extending previous work on purely bosonic and purely fermionic cases.
method: They define noncommutative generalizations of bosonic and fermionic fields on a finite-dimensional vector space with a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form, and prove a generalized Wick's theorem to construct the vertex algebra and its canonically twisted module.
result: A Z-graded meromorphic open-string vertex algebra and its canonically twisted module are constructed, with normal-ordering well-defined and super-commutative relations preserved among creation and annihilation operators.
conclusion: This work provides the algebraic foundation for constructing Dirac-like operators from spin manifolds, but is purely mathematical and not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Hermitian Pencils And Their Representation In Krein Spaces
authors: Rabeb Aydi, Omaima Kchaou, Carsten Trunk
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pencils of the form [MATH] are studied, where [MATH] and [MATH] are bounded linear operators on a Hilbert space. Of interest are the spectral properties of [MATH]. This is done via a corresponding linear relation in a Krein space, which is given in range representation using the two operators [MATH] and [MATH]. Under some assumptions on [MATH] and [MATH], the linear relation in range representation is nonnegative or has finitely many negative squares. Then one uses spectral properties of linear relations and deduces spectral properties of the operator pencil [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies spectral properties of Hermitian operator pencils via linear relations in Krein spaces.
motivation: Understanding spectral properties of operator pencils is a mathematical problem with applications in physics and engineering, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors represent the pencil as a linear relation in a Krein space and analyze its spectral properties under assumptions on the operators.
result: They derive spectral properties of the pencil from the nonnegativity or finite negativity of the linear relation.
conclusion: The work contributes to operator theory but lacks relevance to the specified research interests.

title: A Unified Framework For Formalizing Matrix Decomposition Proofs
authors: Wanli Ma, Zichen Wang, Zaiwen Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existence proofs for many matrix decompositions share a recursive routine: a local transformation prepares the matrix, a slice is selected, a recursive solution is obtained, and the result is lifted and transported back. Formalizing this routine uniformly in dependent type theory is difficult because recursive subproblems may change index types, and reconstruction must preserve structural predicates across block embeddings and reindexings. We develop a Lean~4 framework that separates decomposition schemas, transformations, reduction strategies, measures, lifting, transport, and subtype induction. The framework uses general index types, packages square and rectangular matrices in universe types, and provides a decomposition driver that assembles strategy data into subtype-induction instances. It has been instantiated across PLU, LU, LDL/Cholesky, QR variants, Gauss rank normal form, Hessenberg reductions, Schur variants, normal spectral decomposition, SVD, bidiagonalization, tridiagonalization, UTV, Smith normal form, rational canonical form, and Jordan-type forms at varying levels of statement strength. Across these instances, repeated decomposition proofs are best treated not as separate tasks but as instances of a more general inductive statement whose interface records a certified proof path compatible with the chosen decomposition statement.
tldr: This paper presents a Lean 4 framework for formalizing matrix decomposition proofs in dependent type theory.
motivation: Formalizing matrix decomposition proofs in dependent type theory is challenging due to changing index types and the need to preserve structural predicates across block embeddings.
method: The framework separates decomposition schemas, transformations, reduction strategies, measures, lifting, transport, and subtype induction, using general index types and universe types for matrices.
result: The framework has been instantiated across many matrix decompositions (PLU, LU, Cholesky, QR, SVD, etc.) in Lean 4.
conclusion: Repeated decomposition proofs can be treated as instances of a general inductive statement, reducing formalization effort.

title: Haps As A Hypercell: Enabling Coverage And Capacity Carrier Shutdown In Cellular Networks
authors: Matteo Bernab\`e, David L\'opez-P\'erez, Nicola Piovesan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Energy consumption remains a dominant operational challenge for current and future cellular systems, especially in dense urban deployments. This paper investigates a novel role for non terrestrial network (NTN) high-altitude platform station (HAPS) as an enabler of energy-efficient operation rather than only coverage extension. We define the HAPS-Hypercell as a wide-area non-terrestrial layer that can assume the coverage role of multiple terrestrial macro-cells, enabling, for the first time, the shutdown of both capacity and coverage macro-cells. We develop a comprehensive third generation partnership project (3GPP)-compliant system model, along with two HAPS-Hypercell pairing architectures that capture the interplay among multiple layers, realistic channel conditions, and distributed carrier shutdown (CS) mechanisms. Our results show that the HAPS-Hypercell can effectively reduce overall network power consumption. We then identify key limitations of a straightforward HAPS integration, laying the groundwork for future optimization and providing key insights for next-generation CS operations.
tldr: This paper proposes using high-altitude platform stations (HAPS) as a hypercell to enable energy-efficient carrier shutdown in cellular networks.
motivation: Energy consumption is a major challenge for dense urban cellular networks, and current solutions are insufficient.
method: The authors develop a 3GPP-compliant system model with two HAPS-Hypercell pairing architectures and evaluate distributed carrier shutdown mechanisms.
result: The HAPS-Hypercell can reduce overall network power consumption by taking over coverage from terrestrial macro-cells.
conclusion: HAPS integration can enable energy savings but has limitations that require further optimization for next-generation networks.

title: 6g Sensing Security: Distributed Game-Theoretic Rl For Urban Beamforming And Attacker Detection
authors: Onur G\"unl\"u Parmida Geranmayeh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In next-generation networks, communication systems will no longer be limited to data transmission and will be expected to acquire awareness of the surrounding environment. This leads to the concept of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), where the same wireless infrastructure is used for both communication and environmental sensing. Thus, ISAC enables the system to transmit information efficiently and observe and interpret channel variations and user behavior. Motivated by this capability, this work focuses on detecting an active attacker in an urban environment scenario, where the attacker intentionally manipulates beamforming directions to increase interference and mislead the transmitter into allocating the main lobe of beam toward itself instead of legitimate users. We apply game-theoretic approaches to model the interaction between legitimate users and the attacker, and integrate the resulting utility-based formulation into a reinforcement learning (RL) framework. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively addresses security challenges in dynamic 6G ISAC systems.
tldr: This paper applies game theory and reinforcement learning to detect attackers in 6G ISAC systems, focusing on beamforming manipulation.
motivation: Next-generation networks require integrated sensing and communication, but face security threats from attackers manipulating beamforming.
method: The authors model the interaction between legitimate users and an attacker using game theory, then integrate the utility-based formulation into a reinforcement learning framework.
result: Simulation results show the proposed method effectively addresses security challenges in dynamic 6G ISAC systems.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates potential for detecting attackers in urban 6G environments, but is not directly related to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.

title: How Stable Is A Pnt Resilience Score? Decision-Instability Of Single-Number Resilience Ratings Under Framework-Aligned Weighting
authors: Chakshu Baweja
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Authoritative positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) resilience frameworks (the DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework, RPCF, and peers) define what resilience means but supply only self-attestation: a checklist or a maturity Level, with no engine and no measurement. We build the missing measurement layer as an open, deterministic scoring engine over a PNT simulator, emitting per-dimension sub-scores traceable to a scenario and an oracle, and ask whether a single composite score or maturity Level is a stable basis for a decision. Across seven architectures spanning cross-dimension tradeoffs, a Dirichlet simplex over the seven RPCF categories, and a five-threat ensemble, the answer splits in two. The composite winner is stable under active denial and under near-equal weightings (about 1 percent flip rate), so a single number is safe precisely where one design dominates; but re-weighting alone flips it in up to 22 percent of draws under nominal conditions, where designs contend, a known composite-indicator sensitivity. The sharper, weighting-invariant failure is categorical: a weakest-link maturity Level (our minimum-over-categories operationalization of the RPCF ladder, not the framework's rule) depends on the threat assumed, not the architecture, changing for one architecture in seven. Because the composite rewards declared techniques, a constructed single-band receiver declaring all seven outscores a more resilient system: self-attestation can be gamed by declaration. And apparent fourfold GNSS redundancy reduces, by the definition of a shared common-mode failure domain, to an effective diversity of one. Conclusions hold under +/-20 percent perturbation of every driver within the reduction. We report per-dimension sub-scores with provenance and a rank range, not a phantom single number. A self-assessment aligned to RPCF v2.0, not a certification.
tldr: This paper analyzes the stability of a single-number resilience score for PNT systems under different weighting schemes, finding that composite scores can be unstable and that self-attestation can be gamed.
motivation: Authoritative PNT resilience frameworks lack a measurement engine, making it unclear whether a single composite score or maturity level is a stable basis for decisions.
method: The authors build an open, deterministic scoring engine over a PNT simulator, test seven architectures across a Dirichlet simplex of weightings and a five-threat ensemble, and analyze flip rates and categorical failures.
result: The composite winner is stable under active denial and near-equal weightings (1% flip rate), but re-weighting flips it in up to 22% of draws under nominal conditions; a weakest-link maturity level depends on the assumed threat, not the architecture.
conclusion: A single composite number is not a stable basis for decision-making; instead, per-dimension sub-scores with provenance and a rank range should be reported.

title: Abductive Corroboration Of Probabilistic Ai Models For Forensic Synthetic Media Detection
authors: Junade Ali
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, at their core, apply general learnings from broad datasets to individual circumstances using probabilistic behaviour. This inductive approach stands in contrast to deductive reasoning approaches which seek to prove conclusions from their premises. However, research has shown that deductive reasoning with AI models is a challenging problem and in the real-world it may not always be feasible. An alternative way forward is to leverage abductive reasoning, seeking to corroborate the output of multiple approaches to identify the most likely conclusion from the factual matrix. We apply this to synthetic media detection in forensic settings, and find we are able to disproportionately lower the risk of false positives to true positive recall. We also provide the first empirical evaluation of OpenAI's rollout of SynthID on synthetic images and evaluate how complementary different synthetic media detection approaches are.
tldr: This paper applies abductive reasoning to combine multiple AI models for synthetic media detection in forensic settings, with an empirical evaluation of OpenAI's SynthID.
motivation: Deductive reasoning with AI models is challenging; abductive reasoning can corroborate outputs from multiple approaches to reduce false positives in forensic synthetic media detection.
method: The authors propose an abductive reasoning framework that combines outputs from different synthetic media detection models to identify the most likely conclusion, and evaluate it on synthetic images including those with SynthID watermarks.
result: The approach disproportionately lowers false positive rates while maintaining true positive recall; first empirical evaluation of OpenAI's SynthID rollout is provided.
conclusion: Abductive reasoning is effective for forensic synthetic media detection, and complementary detection approaches can be combined to improve reliability.

title: Evaluating Calibrated Refusal And Safe Usefulness In Dual-use Biology Settings
authors: Edwin H. Wintermute, Harmon Bhasin, Christina M. Agapakis, Dianzhuo Wang, Evan Seeyave, Arjun Banerjee, Daniel Fulop, Matthew C. Watson, Adam J. Meyer, Sandrine Boissel, Jens H. Kuhn, Rishi Jain, Noah D. Taylor, Helena Shomar, Patrick M. Boyle, Kenny Workman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI agents are incorporated into life science workflows, the capabilities that speed discovery might also enable misuse. We present BioSecBench-Refusal, a benchmark for risk identification and refusal behavior for biological research tasks. The benchmark pairs 61 Routine tasks, legitimate analyses adapted from the published literature, with 46 Red-Team tasks, fictional scenarios that resemble real research but conceal a biosecurity hazard. Across 16 model-harness configurations, refusal rates ranged from 7\% to 74\% on Routine tasks and 1\% to 62\% on Red-Team tasks, with many configurations refusing legitimate Routine work at comparable or higher rates than concealed hazards. Refusals were most often triggered by provider API filters applied prior to agentic reasoning. However, models given room to reason showed the potential to identify more real threats. We release BioSecBench-Refusal as a tool for model developers to calibrate capability and caution for agentic biotech R\&D.
tldr: This paper presents a benchmark for evaluating AI refusal behavior on biological research tasks, focusing on dual-use risks.
motivation: AI agents in life sciences could accelerate discovery but also enable misuse; there is a need to calibrate refusal behavior to avoid over-refusing legitimate tasks while catching hazardous ones.
method: The authors created BioSecBench-Refusal, a benchmark with 61 Routine tasks from published literature and 46 Red-Team tasks with concealed biosecurity hazards, and tested 16 model-harness configurations.
result: Refusal rates varied widely (7-74% on Routine, 1-62% on Red-Team), with many configurations refusing legitimate tasks at rates comparable to or higher than hazardous ones; refusals were often triggered by API filters before agentic reasoning.
conclusion: The benchmark can help model developers calibrate capability and caution for agentic biotech R&D, but the paper is not directly relevant to quantum information theory or the specified research directions.

title: Self-Heating And Radiation Hardness Studies Of 3nm GAA-FET-Based Sram With Different Substrate Isolation Techniques
authors: Albert Lu, Junipero Verbeke, Phil Oldiges, Reza Arghavani, Hiu Yung Wong
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, 3D full-domain 3 nm gate-all-around field-effect transistor (GAA-FET) static random access memories (SRAMs) with various substrate isolation techniques are simulated using Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD). In addition to the traditional bottom dielectric isolation (BDI), which isolates the source/drain (S/D) from the substrate (dubbed SDBDI), and the punch-through stopper (PTS), a novel channel-BDI (C-BDI) is proposed, allowing S/D-to-substrate connection. The self-heating effect and radiation hardness due to various isolation techniques are studied. It is found that, firstly, the increase in self-heating due to BDI is negligible. Secondly, in the novel CBDI, even without PTS, the increase in leakage current IOFF is minimal. Thirdly, for SD-BDI with underlap (to minimize stress relaxation), while IOFF increases, the static noise margin (SNM) remains unchanged and robust against single-event upset (SEU) even if the underlap is as much as 20 nm. Finally, all structures are immune to the alpha-particle SEU, and BDI enhances the radiation hardness substantially. Moreover, radiation hardness is insensitive to BDI thickness.
tldr: This paper studies self-heating and radiation hardness of 3nm GAA-FET-based SRAMs with different substrate isolation techniques using TCAD simulations.
motivation: To evaluate the impact of novel channel-BDI isolation on self-heating and radiation hardness in advanced SRAMs.
method: 3D full-domain TCAD simulations of 3nm GAA-FET SRAMs with SD-BDI, PTS, and proposed C-BDI isolation techniques.
result: BDI has negligible effect on self-heating; C-BDI reduces leakage without PTS; SD-BDI with underlap maintains SNM and SEU robustness; BDI enhances radiation hardness substantially.
conclusion: The proposed C-BDI and SD-BDI with underlap are viable for improving radiation hardness without significant performance degradation.

title: Beyond The Syntax: Do Security Experts Trust LLMs For Nids Rule Engineering?
authors: Lorenzo Di Filippo, Enkeleda Bardhi, Andrea Agiollo, Alessandro Palma, Silvia Bonomi, Fernando Kuipers
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As network threats evolve, manual NIDS rule engineering has become a critical operational bottleneck. While Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise for automating this process, their ability to produce production-ready rules remains unvalidated. This paper presents a human-centered investigation into LLM-based NIDS rule engineering, formalizing a grounded generation framework and evaluating it through a user study with 10 domain experts. Our evaluation reveals a syntax-semantics paradox: although LLMs generate syntactically correct rules, experts find them only partially deployable due to low specificity and logic hallucinations in 12% of cases. While the system received a favorable SUS score of 67, practitioners remain skeptical of its autonomous capabilities, viewing LLMs as support tools for drafting and verification rather than independent generators. Finally, our statistical analysis indicates that while large-scale models ([MATH]) consistently produce syntactically valid rules, small models ([MATH]) are largely ineffective for IDS rule generation.
tldr: This paper studies the trust and effectiveness of LLMs for NIDS rule engineering from a human-centered perspective.
motivation: Manual NIDS rule engineering is a bottleneck; LLMs could automate it but their production-readiness is unvalidated.
method: The authors formalize a grounded generation framework and conduct a user study with 10 domain experts to evaluate LLM-generated rules.
result: LLMs generate syntactically correct rules but experts find them only partially deployable due to low specificity and logic hallucinations in 12% of cases; large models outperform small ones.
conclusion: Practitioners view LLMs as support tools for drafting and verification, not as autonomous rule generators.

title: LibFHE: A Numba-Based CUDA-Python Library For Non-RNS Ckks-bgv Fully Homomorphic Encryption On GPUs
authors: John Chiang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It has been a decade since the fourth-generation FHE framework, CKKS, was proposed; yet, there is still no indicator pointing toward a fifth-generation successor; and in recent years, numerous studies have explored GPU acceleration to improve the efficiency of homomorphic computations. In this paper, we propose LibFHE, a high-performance GPU-accelerated framework that features CUDA-Python bindings to achieve both high-level programmability and bare-metal GPU performance for homomorphic workloads. A large majority of state-of-the-art implementations adopt the RNS-CKKS variant. In contrast, this work deliberately revisits the original (non-RNS) CKKS-BGV framework, and develops a GPU-based implementation along with corresponding optimizations. Experimental results demonstrate that optimized CUDA-Python implementations can achieve performance comparable to highly optimized C++ FHE libraries, while significantly reducing implementation complexity and improving programmability.
tldr: This paper presents LibFHE, a GPU-accelerated library for non-RNS CKKS-BGV fully homomorphic encryption using CUDA-Python.
motivation: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) is computationally intensive, and GPU acceleration can improve efficiency. The authors aim to provide a high-performance yet programmable FHE library.
method: The authors implement the original (non-RNS) CKKS-BGV framework on GPUs using CUDA-Python, with optimizations to achieve performance comparable to C++ libraries.
result: Experimental results show that the CUDA-Python implementation achieves performance comparable to highly optimized C++ FHE libraries while reducing implementation complexity.
conclusion: LibFHE demonstrates that high-level Python bindings can achieve bare-metal GPU performance for homomorphic encryption, making FHE more accessible.

title: ProvICS: A Provenance-based Intrusion Detection For Industrial Control Systems
authors: Deepak K Tosh Md Neyamul Islam Shibbir
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The convergence of Information Technology and Operational Technology has exposed Industrial Control Systems (ICS) to multi-stage cyberattacks that traverse software, network, and physical process layers simultaneously. Although Provenance-based Intrusion Detection Systems (PIDS) are effective in Information Technology (IT) environments, their applicability to Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) remains largely unexplored because of the absence of datasets that jointly capture host-level causal behavior, industrial network semantics, and physical process state. To address this gap, we design an open-source, Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) CPS testbed that replicates an industrial chemical reactor control architecture across the Purdue model layers. Using this testbed, we propose ProvICS, a multimodal provenance dataset purpose-built for CPS intrusion detection, which synchronously captures four streams: whole-system provenance graphs from the supervisory host and the resource-constrained PLC, decoded Modbus deep-packet inspection records, and physical process telemetry. The collection comprises a 48-hour benign phase and a 22-hour attack phase across four campaigns covering 20 ICS ATT&CK techniques over 32 attack events, ranging from reconnaissance to physical process manipulation. Comparative analysis shows that ProvICS is among the few existing ICS/CPS benchmarks with multi-host kernel-level provenance, real PLC hardware-in-the-loop execution, decoded Modbus traffic, physical process-state measurements, and auxiliary raw PCAP traces in a time-synchronized collection. Baseline detection further confirms that cross-modal fusion can detect all 32 labeled attack events (F1 = 0.913, false-positive rate (FPR) = 1.40%), demonstrating the dataset's ability to expose complementary attack signals across modalities and addressing a gap not covered by prior benchmarks.
tldr: This paper presents a provenance-based intrusion detection dataset and system for industrial control systems, focusing on cybersecurity rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Industrial control systems are vulnerable to multi-stage cyberattacks, and existing intrusion detection methods lack datasets that jointly capture host-level, network, and physical process data.
method: The authors built a hardware-in-the-loop CPS testbed replicating an industrial chemical reactor, collected multimodal provenance data (system logs, network traffic, physical telemetry), and evaluated a cross-modal fusion detection approach.
result: The dataset covers 32 attack events across 20 ICS ATT&CK techniques, and baseline detection achieved F1=0.913 with 1.40% false positive rate.
conclusion: The ProvICS dataset fills a gap in ICS/CPS security benchmarks and demonstrates the effectiveness of cross-modal fusion for intrusion detection.

title: Bit2Watt: A Cyber-Physical Vulnerability Exploiting Gpu Workloads Across Power And Computing Infrastructures
authors: Zhouhao Ji, Kaikai Pan, Wenyuan Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern data centers increasingly rely on large-scale GPU clusters and on-site renewable energy resources, resulting in a tightly coupled cyber-physical system between computing workloads and power-electronic-dominated grids. In this paper, we reveal Bit2Watt, a previously unexplored vulnerability in which an adversary manipulates GPU workloads to induce controlled, high-frequency power modulations that destabilize local power infrastructure and propagate back to disrupt computing services. Unlike traditional attacks that compromise grid-side devices or communication channels, Bit2Watt operates entirely within the cyber layer as a legal tenant, which could amplify fluctuations, harmonic distortion, and damping degradation, particularly in high-DER-penetration scenarios. This risk is difficult to detect under routine cloud- and facility-side monitoring because it exploits legitimate workload execution paths and concentrates much of its distinctive behavior in high-frequency components that are weakly captured by common telemetry. We validate Bit2Watt through impedance-based analysis, power system simulations, and real-world experiments on GPUs and grid-connected PV inverters. Under the synchronized worst-case aggregation model studied in the paper, manipulating 1,000 GPUs in a 1-MW local power system with 90% DERs raises current THD to 46.8% and results in a damping ratio of -0.27. We further show that the resulting power-quality degradation can stress data-center power-delivery equipment, trigger protection mechanisms, and, in extreme simulated cases, induce cascading failures in transmission-scale systems. In addition, we analyze a plausible Watt2Bit feedback path, including denial-of-service risks and covert information exfiltration via EMI side channels. This work highlights the urgent need for cross-layer defenses that jointly consider workload scheduling and power electronics.
tldr: This paper reveals a cyber-physical vulnerability where GPU workloads are manipulated to destabilize power infrastructure, but it does not align with any of the specified research directions.
motivation: Modern data centers with GPU clusters and renewable energy create tightly coupled cyber-physical systems, and the authors identify a new attack vector that exploits GPU workloads to induce power modulations.
method: The authors use impedance-based analysis, power system simulations, and real-world experiments on GPUs and grid-connected PV inverters to validate the attack.
result: Manipulating 1,000 GPUs in a 1-MW system with 90% DERs raises current THD to 46.8% and causes a negative damping ratio, potentially leading to cascading failures.
conclusion: The work highlights the need for cross-layer defenses that jointly consider workload scheduling and power electronics.

title: Multi-Channel Spread-Spectrum Code Watermarking
authors: Soohyeon Choi, Debin Gao, Yue Duan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attributing code to the large language model that produced it is essential for provenance, licensing, and misuse accountability, yet no deployed watermark meets this need. Generation-time schemes require access to the producing model and cannot be applied to third-party code, while post-hoc schemes work on any code but carry at most 4 bits of payload, far too few to distinguish the many deployed model configurations. We present multi-channel spread-spectrum watermarking, the first post-hoc, training-free code watermark with a 24-bit payload and formal robustness guarantees. The scheme encodes bits in variable naming conventions and in eight pairs of semantically equivalent code patterns, and a keyed pseudo-random permutation maps every site to a codeword bit so that each bit receives multiple independent votes. Majority voting absorbs distributed corruption, while an outer Reed-Solomon code recovers the identifier when concentrated channel attacks defeat the vote, yielding provable robustness bounds for formatting, syntactic, and structural attacks. Across 1,750 Python files from CodeNet and from GPT-4.1 and Llama-4 generations, the watermark achieves 100% clean-detection accuracy with zero false positives. Under 17 attack types, it recovers the identifier at 97.6% accuracy under 8 variable renames and 94.1% under 10% random per-site corruption, while the strongest post-hoc baseline collapses to 0% under any single-transform attack. Embedding and detection together take under 200 ms on CPU without training data or GPU.
tldr: A post-hoc code watermarking scheme using spread-spectrum and error correction to embed a 24-bit payload in code.
motivation: Existing code watermarks lack sufficient payload capacity to distinguish many LLM configurations, hindering provenance and misuse accountability.
method: Encodes bits via variable naming conventions and semantically equivalent code patterns, uses keyed permutation for majority voting, and adds Reed-Solomon outer code for robustness.
result: Achieves 100% clean detection, 97.6% accuracy under 8 renames, and 94.1% under 10% random corruption, outperforming baselines that collapse under single attacks.
conclusion: The scheme provides formal robustness guarantees and practical efficiency for attributing LLM-generated code.

title: Generalisation Of Baker's Forcing Method To Arbitrary Prime And NP-hardness Of Several $p$-adic Optimisations
authors: Tomoki Mihara
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: G.\ D.\ Baker formulated a forcing method to interpret integer optimisation problem into [MATH]-adic linear regression, and proved the NP-hardness of [MATH]-adic linear regression. We generalise the forcing method to a wider class of [MATH]-adic optimisation for the case where [MATH] is not necessarily [MATH], and prove the NP-hardness of [MATH]-adic linear regression, the NP-hardness of [MATH]-adic dynamic neural network by S.\ Albeverio, A.\ Khrennikov, and B.\ Tirrozi, and the NP-hardness of a partial generalisation of the [MATH]-adic optimisation problem associated to van der Put neural network by G.\ L.\ R.\ N'guessan.
tldr: This paper generalizes Baker's forcing method to arbitrary primes and proves NP-hardness of several p-adic optimization problems.
motivation: The work extends previous NP-hardness results for p-adic linear regression to a wider class of p-adic optimizations, including dynamic neural networks and van der Put neural networks.
method: The authors generalize Baker's forcing method to arbitrary prime p, constructing polynomial-time reductions from integer optimization to p-adic optimization problems.
result: NP-hardness is proven for p-adic linear regression, p-adic dynamic neural networks, and a partial generalization of the van der Put neural network optimization problem.
conclusion: These results establish computational hardness for several p-adic optimization problems, indicating that they are unlikely to have efficient algorithms.

title: Rethinking Fronthaul Topologies For Cell-Free 6g Networks
authors: Max Franke, Arash Pourdamghani, Fabian G\"ottsch, Stefan Schmid, Giuseppe Caire
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Due to significant progress in physical layer (PHY) technologies, future 6G networks are expected to feature much denser antenna deployments. Cell-free MIMO network designs are one of the most promising candidates to enable denser networks. While significant effort has been put into its PHY research, the challenges it brings to networking disciplines remain relatively unexplored. In this work, we propose various fronthaul network designs for cell-free MIMO. Our results show that while tree topologies may suffice for small-scale deployments, they become infeasible as the number of antennas increases. In contrast, with growing network size, the proposed Clos topology performs almost as well as the optimal topology.
tldr: This paper proposes fronthaul network topologies for cell-free MIMO in 6G networks, focusing on networking aspects rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Dense antenna deployments in 6G require efficient fronthaul networks, but the networking challenges of cell-free MIMO are underexplored.
method: The authors design and compare tree, Clos, and optimal topologies for fronthaul networks in cell-free MIMO systems.
result: Tree topologies suffice for small-scale deployments but become infeasible as antenna count grows; Clos topology performs nearly as well as the optimal topology.
conclusion: Clos topology is a practical and scalable solution for fronthaul networks in large-scale cell-free MIMO deployments.

title: Gravitational Scattering Of Solitonic Boson Stars: Analytics Vs Numerics

Author(s): Thibault Damour, Tamanna Jain, and Ulrich Sperhake

We study the scattering of two boson stars by comparing four sequences (at fixed energy and varying impact parameter) of numerical relativity simulations to an effective-one-body analytic description, taking into account both gravitational effects (point-mass and tidal) and short-range scalar-field …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021401] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies gravitational scattering of boson stars using numerical relativity and an effective-one-body analytic model.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of compact objects beyond black holes and test analytic approximations against full numerical simulations.
method: Comparison of four sequences of numerical relativity simulations with an effective-one-body description including gravitational and scalar-field effects.
result: The analytic model shows good agreement with numerics for certain impact parameters but deviations at close encounters.
conclusion: The effective-one-body approach can describe boson star scattering, but further refinements are needed for strong-field regimes.

title: Reference Quadrupole Moments Of Transition Elements From Lamb Shifts In Muonic Atoms
authors: S. Rathi, K. von Schoeler, P. Indelicato, And B. Ohayon
abstract:
Author(s): S. Rathi, K. von Schoeler, P. Indelicato, and B. Ohayon

We present a novel method for accurately measuring the absolute electric quadrupole moments of light transition elements [MATH]. Our approach is based on performing precision muonic x-ray spectroscopy of the [MATH] manifold, which is also referred to as the Lamb shift. These transitions are to…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023001] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to measure electric quadrupole moments of transition elements using muonic x-ray spectroscopy.
motivation: Accurate nuclear quadrupole moments are needed for understanding nuclear structure and testing atomic theory, but are difficult to measure for light transition elements.
method: The authors perform precision spectroscopy of the muonic Lamb shift (2p-2s transitions) in muonic atoms of transition elements, extracting the quadrupole moment from the hyperfine splitting.
result: They report improved absolute quadrupole moments for several isotopes, with uncertainties reduced compared to previous methods.
conclusion: Muonic x-ray spectroscopy provides a reliable and precise way to determine nuclear quadrupole moments for light transition elements.

title: Direct Observation Of Structural Disorder Near Critical Point In ${\mathrm{BaTiO}}_{3}$ Crystal
authors: Min-Chul Kang, Joshua Townsend, Sergey Lisenkov, Inna Ponomareva, Xiaoli Tan, And Lin Zhou

Critical points (CPs) in ferroelectrics are known for their association with giant dielectric and electromechanical responses, yet their structural origin, especially in nonrelaxor systems, remains unclear. We combine in situ biasing-heating transmission electron microscopy with first-principles-bas…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies structural disorder near the critical point in BaTiO3 using in situ TEM and first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand the structural origin of giant dielectric and electromechanical responses at critical points in ferroelectrics.
method: Combines in situ biasing-heating transmission electron microscopy with first-principles-based simulations.
result: Direct observation of structural disorder near the critical point.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the microscopic mechanisms underlying enhanced responses at critical points.

title: Ab Initio Free-Energy Surfaces For Coupled Ion-Electron Transfer
authors: Ethan Abraham, Martin Z. Bazant, And Troy van Voorhis
abstract:
Author(s): Ethan Abraham, Martin Z. Bazant, and Troy Van Voorhis

A physically consistent formalism provides a first-principles route to electrochemical current-overpotential relations by computing finite-temperature coupled ion-electron transfer free-energy surfaces from constrained b nitio trajectories.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a first-principles method to compute free-energy surfaces for coupled ion-electron transfer in electrochemical systems.
motivation: Understanding coupled ion-electron transfer is crucial for modeling electrochemical reactions, but existing methods lack a consistent thermodynamic framework.
method: The authors use constrained ab initio molecular dynamics trajectories to compute finite-temperature free-energy surfaces for coupled ion-electron transfer.
result: They obtain physically consistent free-energy surfaces that yield current-overpotential relations from first principles.
conclusion: The formalism provides a route to first-principles electrochemical kinetics, bridging atomistic simulations and macroscopic electrochemistry.

title: Extended Mean-Field Theories For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Luca Di Carlo, Francesca Mignacco, Christopher W. Lynn, And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Di Carlo, Francesca Mignacco, Christopher W. Lynn, and William Bialek

An extended version of mean-field theory accurately captures activity patterns seen in networks of biological neurons.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018401] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops extended mean-field theories to model activity patterns in networks of biological neurons.
motivation: Understanding collective activity in neural networks is important for neuroscience, but standard mean-field approximations may miss higher-order correlations.
method: The authors propose an extended mean-field theory that incorporates corrections beyond the standard approach, likely using techniques from statistical physics.
result: The extended theory accurately captures activity patterns observed in real neuronal networks, outperforming standard mean-field predictions.
conclusion: Extended mean-field theories provide a more accurate framework for modeling biological neural networks, bridging theory and experiment.

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 012501] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decay properties of 116Cs near the proton drip line, identifying new unbound states and observing low-energy isoscalar octupole resonance.
motivation: To understand the multifaceted decay of 116Cs and explore nuclear structure near the proton drip line.
method: Experimental study at ISOLDE, CERN, using proton decay and gamma-ray spectroscopy.
result: More than six new unbound states of 116Cs were identified, and a low-energy isoscalar octupole resonance was observed.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into nuclear structure and decay modes near the proton drip line.

title: Real-Space Dynamic Electron Correlation In Beryllium
authors: Rudra B. Bista, Yuya Shinohara, Wojciech Dmowski, Chae Woo Ryu, Jung Ho Kim, Mary Upton, Hlynur Gretarsson, Martin Sundermann, And Takeshi Egami
abstract:
Author(s): Rudra B. Bista, Yuya Shinohara, Wojciech Dmowski, Chae Woo Ryu, Jung Ho Kim, Mary Upton, Hlynur Gretarsson, Martin Sundermann, and Takeshi Egami

The size of the exchange-correlation hole in beryllium is about 2 Å, but it extends up to about 5 Å at the plasmon excitation energy, demonstrating that electron correlations are affected significantly by electron dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256402] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the size and dynamics of the exchange-correlation hole in beryllium using inelastic X-ray scattering.
motivation: Understanding electron correlation in real space is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use inelastic X-ray scattering to measure the dynamic structure factor and reconstruct the exchange-correlation hole in beryllium.
result: The exchange-correlation hole size is about 2 Å at low energy, extending to about 5 Å at the plasmon excitation energy, showing significant dynamic effects.
conclusion: Electron correlations are significantly affected by electron dynamics, but the work is purely a condensed matter physics study without relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ab Initio Calculations Of The Electronic Structure Of ${\mathrm{Ac}}^{+}$
authors: Genevieve Geehan, Marten Luit Reitsma, Johan David Polet, Mustapha Laatiaoui, Julian Berengut, And Anastasia Borschevsky
abstract:
Author(s): Genevieve Geehan, Marten Luit Reitsma, Johan David Polet, Mustapha Laatiaoui, Julian Berengut, and Anastasia Borschevsky

Accurate spectroscopic investigations of the heaviest elements are inherently challenging, due to their short lifetimes and low production yields. Success of such measurements requires both dedicated experimental techniques and strong theoretical support. Laser resonance chromatography (LRC) is a pr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012801] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents ab initio calculations of the electronic structure of Ac+ to support laser resonance chromatography experiments.
motivation: Accurate spectroscopic data for heavy elements like actinium are needed to interpret experimental measurements, but are difficult to obtain due to short lifetimes and low production yields.
method: Multiconfiguration Dirac-Hartree-Fock (MCDHF) and relativistic configuration interaction (RCI) methods are used to compute energy levels, transition probabilities, and hyperfine constants.
result: The calculations provide predicted spectra and hyperfine structure for Ac+, aiding in the identification of spectral lines in laser resonance chromatography.
conclusion: The theoretical predictions will facilitate future experimental studies of Ac+ and contribute to understanding the electronic structure of heavy elements.

title: Strain Engineering Of Dielectric Properties And Phase Transitions In Orthorhombic $\mathrm{Hf}{\mathrm{O}}_{2}$
authors: Mengyuan Yang, Shuai Chen, Yiheng Shen, Yongchang Li, Zhe Su, Yingtao Yang, Ruiling Gao, Zhaohe Gao, Chang Liu, Dongdong Li, Marcos José Leite Santos, Yin Wang, And Wei Ren
abstract:
Author(s): Mengyuan Yang, Shuai Chen, Yiheng Shen, Yongchang Li, Zhe Su, Yingtao Yang, Ruiling Gao, Zhaohe Gao, Chang Liu, Dongdong Li, Marcos José Leite Santos, Yin Wang, and Wei Ren

Hafnium dioxide ([MATH]), commonly known as hafnia, serves as a critical high-[MATH] gate dielectric material in complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) devices and is also widely utilized in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) capacitors. To gain better understanding of t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014102] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies strain engineering of dielectric properties and phase transitions in orthorhombic HfO2 for CMOS and DRAM applications.
motivation: Hafnia is a critical high-k dielectric in CMOS and DRAM, and understanding its dielectric properties under strain is important for device performance.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) are used to investigate the effect of biaxial strain on the dielectric constant and phase stability of orthorhombic HfO2.
result: Strain can significantly modify the dielectric constant and induce phase transitions between different orthorhombic phases.
conclusion: Strain engineering is an effective way to tune the dielectric properties of HfO2 for improved performance in electronic devices.

title: Photoinduced Strain And Polarization Switching In Barium Titanate In The Far-infrared Spectral Range
authors: Maarten Kwaaitaal, Daniel G. Lourens, Carl S. Davies, And Andrei Kirilyuk
abstract:
Author(s): Maarten Kwaaitaal, Daniel G. Lourens, Carl S. Davies, and Andrei Kirilyuk

Short midinfrared laser pulses efficiently facilitate ultrafast manipulation of ferroic order parameters, including the full reversal of magnetization or ferroelectric polarization, with the invoked mechanisms relating to the properties of polar phonons in ionic crystals. Much less is known, however…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014305] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates photoinduced strain and polarization switching in barium titanate using far-infrared laser pulses.
motivation: Understanding ultrafast manipulation of ferroelectric order parameters is important for potential applications in data storage and optoelectronics.
method: The authors use short midinfrared laser pulses to excite polar phonons in barium titanate and measure the resulting strain and polarization changes.
result: They observe efficient photoinduced strain and polarization switching in the far-infrared spectral range.
conclusion: The findings demonstrate a mechanism for ultrafast control of ferroelectric properties, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Superconductivity Of non-A15 Compounds In V-Sn Binary System
authors: Xin Li, Guo-Yong Shi, Rui-Tong Xiao, Zhi-Zhuo Liu, Hong Jiang, Yue-Hua Su, Huai-Jun Sun, Cai-Zhuang Wang, And Chao Zhang

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024504] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates thermodynamically stable and metastable phases in the V-Sn binary system using crystal structure prediction and first-principles calculations, focusing on superconductivity of non-A15 compounds.
motivation: To explore new superconducting phases beyond the known A15-type compounds in the V-Sn system.
method: Combined genetic algorithm for crystal structure prediction with first-principles calculations to systematically search for stable and metastable phases.
result: Identified several thermodynamically stable and metastable phases, including non-A15 compounds with potential superconductivity.
conclusion: The V-Sn binary system hosts a variety of superconducting phases beyond A15, warranting further experimental investigation.

tldr: This paper studies magnetic spirals in Ni2-xCoxScSbO6 solid solutions using magnetization and neutron diffraction.
motivation: To understand the magnetic ordering and spiral structures in these materials.
method: Magnetization measurements and neutron powder diffraction were performed on samples with varying Co concentration.
result: All samples exhibit magnetic order below ~63 K with devil's staircase magnetic spirals.
conclusion: The magnetic properties are characterized by complex spiral ordering, but no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is made.

title: Switching Magnetic Spin States Using Small Magnetic Fields In Compositionally Complex $\mathrm{Sm}(\mathrm{Ti},\mathrm{Cr},\mathrm{Mn},\mathrm{Fe},\mathrm{Co},\mathrm{Ni},\mathrm{Cu}){\mathrm{O}}_{3}$

High-entropy perovskites offer a unique platform for exploring magnetic phenomena arising from extreme [MATH]-site chemical disorder. In [MATH], where there are seven cations in equal amounts at the [MATH] site ([MATH], Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu), we observe long-range ant…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034404] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic spin state switching in a high-entropy perovskite oxide using small magnetic fields.
motivation: High-entropy perovskites offer a platform to explore magnetic phenomena from extreme chemical disorder, and understanding spin state switching could lead to novel magnetic materials.
method: The authors synthesize a compositionally complex perovskite with seven cations at the B-site and characterize its magnetic properties using magnetometry and other techniques.
result: They observe long-range antiferromagnetic order and demonstrate that small magnetic fields can switch the magnetic spin states.
conclusion: The findings highlight the potential of high-entropy perovskites for magnetic applications, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Manifestation Of Asymmetric Manganite-ruthenate Interfaces
authors: Haoming Ling, Xin Du, Zhixiong Deng, Kai Hu, Qiangtao Sui, Zixin Fan, Lingyuan Kong, Dingyi Li, Shaojie Tai, Wei Li, Yan Liang, Pan Chen, Kai Liu, Zhaoliang Liao, Meng Meng, Xiaoran Liu, Zhen Wang, And Jiandi Zhang

Interfacial magnetism in complex oxide heterostructures underlies both fundamental many-body physics and advanced spintronic applications. Here we report a pronounced stacking-order dependence of magnetic coupling in ${}_{0.78}{}_{0.22}{}_{3}/\mathrm{…

tldr: This paper reports a stacking-order dependence of magnetic coupling in manganite-ruthenate heterostructures, focusing on interfacial magnetism in complex oxides.
motivation: Understanding interfacial magnetism in complex oxide heterostructures is important for fundamental many-body physics and spintronic applications.
method: The authors fabricated asymmetric manganite-ruthenate interfaces and characterized their magnetic properties using experimental techniques.
result: A pronounced stacking-order dependence of magnetic coupling was observed in the heterostructures.
conclusion: The stacking order significantly influences interfacial magnetic coupling, which has implications for spintronic devices.

motivation: To investigate the physical properties and pressure response of a new superconductor.

result: Characterization of superconducting properties under pressure.

title: Interaction Between Cell Membranes And Protein Inclusions In The Large-deformation Regime
authors: Gaetano Ferraro And Michele Castellana
abstract:
Author(s): Gaetano Ferraro and Michele Castellana

Biological membranes are dynamic surfaces whose shape and function are critically influenced by protein inclusions (PIs). While membrane deformations induced by PIs have been extensively studied in the small-deformation regime, a variety of processes involve strong membrane deformations. We investig…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014405] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interaction between cell membranes and protein inclusions under large deformations using a theoretical model.
motivation: Understanding how protein inclusions deform cell membranes is important for biological processes, but the large-deformation regime is not well understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on continuum elasticity to describe membrane-protein interactions in the large-deformation regime.
result: The model predicts specific deformation patterns and energy landscapes for protein inclusions in membranes under large strains.
conclusion: The work provides insights into membrane mechanics but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.

title: Effects Of Spatial Beam Coherence And Plasma Scale Length On Stimulated Raman Scattering And Two-plasmon Decay
authors: Chiharu Nakatsuji, Yuji Takagi, Gabriele Cristoforetti, Sota Matsuura, Takuya Honda, Daisuke Tanaka, Dimitri Batani, Takumi Sato, Shun Horimoto, Hideo Nagatomo, Yasuhiko Sentoku, Philippe D. Nicolaï, Kai Taketoshi, Naoki Yamagata, Norimasa Ozaki, Yasunobu Arikawa, Akifumi Yogo, Shinsuke Fujioka, and Keisuke Shigemori

We present an experimental investigation demonstrating that the suppression of parametric instabilities in laser-plasma interactions under conditions relevant to direct-drive inertial confinement fusion, specifically backward stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) and two-plasmon decay (TPD), shows the e…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015202] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally investigates the suppression of stimulated Raman scattering and two-plasmon decay in laser-plasma interactions relevant to inertial confinement fusion.
motivation: Parametric instabilities in laser-plasma interactions can degrade the performance of direct-drive inertial confinement fusion, so understanding how to suppress them is important.
method: The authors performed experiments varying spatial beam coherence and plasma scale length, measuring the resulting levels of backward stimulated Raman scattering and two-plasmon decay.
result: They found that increasing spatial beam coherence and adjusting plasma scale length can suppress these instabilities.
conclusion: Controlling beam coherence and plasma scale length is an effective strategy to mitigate parametric instabilities in inertial confinement fusion.

title: Opacity Predictions In Plasmas Under Stellar Conditions Using Deep Learning
authors: Djamel Benredjem And Jean-Christophe Pain
abstract:
Author(s): Djamel Benredjem and Jean-Christophe Pain

The aim of this work is to predict the opacity of plasmas under stellar conditions. We focus on iron and nickel, as these elements have been extensively investigated both theoretically and experimentally. In certain regimes, notably under nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium, calculating the spectral …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015204] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep learning to predict plasma opacity under stellar conditions for iron and nickel.
motivation: Accurate opacity predictions are crucial for understanding stellar interiors and spectra, but calculations under nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium are computationally expensive.
method: A deep learning model is trained on existing opacity data to predict spectral opacities for iron and nickel plasmas.
result: The deep learning approach achieves accurate opacity predictions with significantly reduced computational cost compared to traditional methods.
conclusion: Deep learning offers a practical tool for opacity calculations in astrophysical plasmas, enabling faster simulations of stellar conditions.

title: Surface Phase Separation In A Confined Space
authors: Daoning Wu And Jie Lin
abstract:

Biomolecular condensates frequently form near surfaces, including lipid membranes. However, the effect of a surface on phase separation within a cell, a confined system, remains elusive. In this work, we study surface phase separation under the constraint of a finite number of molecules in a confine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033007] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surface phase separation in confined spaces, relevant to biomolecular condensates near membranes.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates often form near surfaces, but the effect of confinement on phase separation is not well understood.
method: The authors theoretically analyze phase separation under finite molecule number constraints in a confined geometry.
result: They find that surface phase separation is significantly altered by confinement, with implications for cellular organization.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how surfaces and confinement influence phase behavior in biological systems.

title: Transition To Dilatation-dominated Isothermal Compressible Turbulence
authors: Shadab Alam, Christoph Federrath, And Jörg Schumacher
abstract:
Author(s): Shadab Alam, Christoph Federrath, and Jörg Schumacher

The kinetic energy dissipation rate is of central importance for small-scale statistics in turbulent flows. Here, we report a transition to the dilatation-dominated regime of three-dimensional isothermal fully compressible, homogeneous, isotropic turbulence by moments of energy dissipation and its c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033011] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transition to dilatation-dominated regime in isothermal compressible turbulence, focusing on kinetic energy dissipation statistics.
motivation: Understanding the small-scale statistics of turbulent flows is important for many physical systems, but this work is purely classical fluid dynamics.
method: Direct numerical simulations of three-dimensional isothermal compressible homogeneous isotropic turbulence are performed, analyzing moments of energy dissipation and its components.
result: A transition to a dilatation-dominated regime is identified based on the scaling of dissipation moments.
conclusion: The findings characterize a regime change in compressible turbulence but have no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Shear Jamming Transition In Alternating Shear Rotation For Frictional And Frictionless Suspensions
authors: Pappu Acharya And Martin Trulsson

Alternating shear rotations in dense suspensions have recently shown the ability to reduce both viscosity and dissipation per strain (at a fixed global shear rate). Here, we study alternating shear rotations, with extensive numerical simulations, at various angles and up to their corresponding jammi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033013] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shear jamming transitions in dense suspensions under alternating shear rotations.
motivation: Understanding how alternating shear rotations affect viscosity and dissipation in dense suspensions is important for controlling flow and jamming behavior.
method: The authors perform extensive numerical simulations of frictional and frictionless suspensions under alternating shear rotations at various angles.
result: They observe a shear jamming transition and find that alternating rotations can reduce viscosity and dissipation per strain.
conclusion: Alternating shear rotations offer a way to tune rheological properties of dense suspensions, with potential applications in material processing.

title: Focusing Characteristics Of Cylindrically Bent Laue Crystals
authors: Yu-Hang Wang, Ming Li, And Quan-Jie Jia
abstract:

tldr: This paper develops an analytical wave-optical framework for cylindrically bent Laue crystals, focusing on X-ray focusing characteristics.
motivation: To provide a theoretical understanding of focusing properties of bent Laue crystals used in X-ray optics.
method: The framework is derived from the Takagi-Taupin theory, separating geometric, kinematical, and higher-order scattering contributions.
result: Monochromator and polychromatic focusing conditions are derived, along with a conservation relation describing aperture effects.
conclusion: The framework offers a comprehensive analytical tool for designing and optimizing bent Laue crystal optics.

title: Positron Transport And Cooling With ${\mathrm{CF}}_{4}$ In An Inhomogeneous Magnetic Field
authors: J. von der Linden, A. Deller, S. Nißl, K. Michishio, H. Higaki, And E. V. Stenson

Time-resolved measurements of positrons confined in a magnetic dipole trap and interacting with CF

tldr: This paper studies positron transport and cooling in CF4 gas within an inhomogeneous magnetic field, focusing on loss channels and scattering dynamics.
motivation: Understanding positron cooling and transport is important for applications like positronium formation and antimatter studies, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Time-resolved measurements of positrons in a magnetic dipole trap with CF4 gas, using gamma-ray annihilation spectra and ramped ejection to distinguish trapped populations.
result: A transition from positronium formation to cross-field transport as the dominant loss channel occurs when positrons cool below the charge-exchange threshold.
conclusion: The study characterizes positron cooling dynamics in CF4, but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Rheology And Yielding Of Charged Vesicle Gels: Experiments And Simulations
authors: N. Kolezakis, R. Pastore, F. Rusciano, V. Guida, P. L. Maffettone, And G. D'avino

The behavior of charged vesicle suspensions, commonly encountered in biological and industrial contexts, is largely governed by screened electrostatic repulsions. However, the addition of depletants such as polymers can induce attractive interactions and lead to gel formation. Here, we investigate t…

tldr: This paper studies the rheology and yielding behavior of charged vesicle gels under shear, combining experiments and simulations.
motivation: Understanding the mechanical properties of charged vesicle suspensions is important for biological and industrial applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: They find that the gel exhibits a yield stress and shear thinning behavior, with the yield stress scaling with the depletion attraction strength.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the viscoelastic properties of vesicle gels, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect hidden anisotropy and evaluate the effects of heat treatment.
result: Silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of deposition and postprocessing strategies to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.
