The signature travels in the commit object's gpgsig header and is already carried, unparsed, in the commit-message field of the WoC commit tables, so the axis is a scan over existing tables rather than a re-read of the object database. Over the V2604 corpus of 5,866,595,698 commits, 17.59% carry a signature (PGP dominant at 98.96%, with a growing minority of SSH and X.509/sigstore signatures), or 1,031,721,316 signed commits. We release the per-commit signature map c2sigFull, a key-to-author graph gated so that shared organization and continuous-integration keys are separated from person keys, and A2trust, a per-identity attestation tier (unsigned, signed, real-world-bound, cross-corpus attested) that extends the published A2cls identity-class dataset. The signature axis is a precision anchor, not a coverage layer: signed commits skew toward recent and security-conscious developers, a population that overlaps the scholarly authors a bibliography join targets. We use the person keys to build a cryptographically grounded alias gold that calibrates the heuristic WoC alias map independently of hand-labeled pairs, and to attach an attestation provenance to science-to-software identity links. All artifacts are released as a self-contained, in dependently hosted replication package keyed to the WoC V2604 collection.
tldr: This paper presents a dataset and analysis of cryptographic commit signatures in the World of Code, focusing on identity trust tiers for software development.
motivation: To distinguish between claimed and attested identities in git commits by leveraging cryptographic signatures, improving identity resolution and trust in software provenance.
method: The authors extract and parse gpgsig headers from the WoC commit corpus, classify signatures by type (PGP, SSH, X.509), and build a key-to-author graph to separate person keys from organizational/CI keys, then define attestation tiers.
result: 17.59% of 5.9 billion commits are signed; they release per-commit signature maps, a key-to-author graph, and per-identity attestation tiers.
conclusion: The signature axis provides a precision anchor for identity resolution, enabling a cryptographically grounded alias gold standard and improving science-to-software identity links.

title: Slack And Budget Breaking In Threshold Team Production
authors: Alejandro Ranchal-Pedrosa Benjamin Marsh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A threshold system completes a public task only after [MATH] verifiable shares are publicly committed. If the honest schedule creates \( \Nstar=\kappa+\Delta \) share opportunities by deadline [MATH], then [MATH] shares are slack such that a coalition delays completion if and only if it withholds at least [MATH] shares. The incentive problem is therefore to price the cheapest sabotage set. Agents receive a direct fee [MATH] per committed share. A delaying coalition may also obtain delay value at most [MATH], and may earn additional fee revenue during recovery after the deadline. Let [MATH] be a pathwise upper bound on the coalition's incremental fee revenue in a recovery slot that completes the task, including any same-slot overshoot. The principal can post a nonnegative completion bounty that depends only on committed shares, uses no deposits or punishments, and expires if completion is late. The optimal rule is uniform, as if completion occurs by [MATH], every admissible horizon share receives [MATH], otherwise no bounty is paid. Full participation is ex-post strongly delay proof exactly when \( (\Delta+1)f+{\Nstar}B \ge L+R_1^+ . \) Equivalently, the exact worst-case budget is \( B^\star = {\Delta+1} \bigl(L+R_1^+-(\Delta+1)f\bigr)^+ . \) The bound is tight for every nonnegative completion measurable bounty, among the [MATH] horizon shares, some [MATH] receive total bounty at most [MATH], and withholding precisely those shares delays completion. The result applies to threshold signatures, data availability certification, coded dissemination, and generic [MATH]-of-[MATH] completion tasks. We also isolate a separate limit, no transfer rule based only on completed shares can remove a final slot race in which a coalition has already observed enough pre-completion shares to act.
tldr: This paper studies incentive design for threshold team production, focusing on slack and budget breaking to prevent sabotage.
motivation: In threshold systems (e.g., threshold signatures, data availability certification), a coalition may delay completion by withholding shares. The principal needs a bounty rule that ensures delay-proof participation without deposits or punishments.
method: The authors model the problem as a game where agents commit shares and receive fees; a delaying coalition can earn delay value and extra fee revenue. They derive conditions for a uniform completion bounty to be ex-post strongly delay proof and compute the worst-case budget.
result: The optimal bounty rule is uniform: if completion occurs by deadline, each horizon share receives a fixed bounty; otherwise none. The exact worst-case budget is given by a formula involving the number of slack shares, fees, delay value, and incremental revenue.
conclusion: The proposed bounty mechanism achieves full participation and is delay-proof under certain conditions, with tight budget bounds. The results apply to various threshold tasks in distributed systems.

title: FDIFormer:Protocol-Aware Transformer Learning For False Data Injection Attack Detection In Smart Grid Networks
authors: Sandara Sathsarani Wijethunga, Muneeb Ul Hassan, Nasrin Sohrabi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Smart grids use communication networks and intelligent electronic devices for reliable, automated power system operation. As these systems become more interconnected, they are increasingly exposed to cyberattacks such as message tampering, false command injection, and denial-of-service attacks. A particularly concerning threat is False Data Injection (FDI), where attackers manipulate communication messages by deleting, modifying, or adding packets. This is especially critical in IEC 61850-based substations, where Generic Object-Oriented Substation Event (GOOSE) messages deliver time-critical protection and control information between devices. Detecting FDI attacks in IEC 61850 GOOSE traffic is challenging because malicious packets closely resemble legitimate communication, and many existing detection methods depend heavily on manually engineered protocol features requiring extensive domain knowledge and limited generalisability. This paper proposes FDIFormer, a feature-engineering-free framework for FDI attack detection using structured textual representations of GOOSE packet sequences and fine-tuned pre-trained Transformer models. The framework converts protocol packets into structured text windows that capture communication behaviour, enabling Transformer models to learn attack-related patterns directly from the data. Evaluated on the QUT-ZSS-2023-GOOSE dataset under a scenario-level three-fold cross-validation strategy, GraphCodeBERT achieves an MCC of 0.595 +/- 0.122, comparable to the strongest feature-engineered baseline, XGBoost (MCC = 0.604 +/- 0.121), while improving MCC by 0.133 over TF-IDF baselines. These findings show that pre-trained Transformer representations offer an effective technique for FDI attack detection in IEC 61850 GOOSE communication without relying on manually engineered protocol features.
tldr: This paper proposes a Transformer-based framework for detecting false data injection attacks in smart grid communication networks.
motivation: Smart grids are vulnerable to cyberattacks like false data injection, and existing detection methods rely on manually engineered features that require domain expertise and lack generalizability.
method: The framework converts IEC 61850 GOOSE packet sequences into structured text windows and fine-tunes pre-trained Transformer models (e.g., GraphCodeBERT) to learn attack patterns directly from data.
result: GraphCodeBERT achieves an MCC of 0.595, comparable to the best feature-engineered baseline (XGBoost, MCC 0.604) and outperforms TF-IDF baselines by 0.133.
conclusion: Pre-trained Transformer representations can effectively detect FDI attacks in GOOSE traffic without manual feature engineering, offering a generalizable approach.

title: Dithered Gaussian Mechanism For Randomness-Efficient Differential Privacy
authors: Rasmus Pagh Nikita P. Kalinin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the dithered Gaussian mechanism, a novel alternative to the discrete Gaussian mechanism for differential privacy that discretizes the private output rather than the noise distribution itself. By interpreting this discretization as post-processing of the Gaussian mechanism, our construction directly inherits the privacy guarantees of the standard Gaussian mechanism while avoiding vulnerabilities caused by finite-precision floating-point outputs. We show that the mechanism is provably randomness-efficient: by sampling the discretized output values directly, the number of high-quality random bits required for privacy can be reduced significantly and made independent of the noise level. This is achieved by separating the randomness into two sources: a high-quality source used for the privacy-critical sampling step, and a high-performance public source, possibly known to the adversary, that supplies the additional randomness needed for randomized discretization. This separation enables the use of cryptographically secure randomness without substantial performance loss. As an application, we study model training with DP-SGD and show that cryptographically secure noise generation with reduced exposure to floating-point vulnerabilities can be achieved with modest practical overhead.
tldr: This paper proposes a dithered Gaussian mechanism for differential privacy that reduces randomness requirements and avoids floating-point vulnerabilities.
motivation: Differential privacy mechanisms often require high-quality randomness and are vulnerable to floating-point attacks; the authors aim to design a randomness-efficient mechanism that is secure against such vulnerabilities.
method: The mechanism discretizes the private output rather than the noise distribution, separating randomness into a high-quality source for privacy-critical sampling and a public source for discretization.
result: The mechanism inherits privacy guarantees of the standard Gaussian mechanism while reducing the number of high-quality random bits needed, making it independent of noise level.
conclusion: The dithered Gaussian mechanism enables cryptographically secure noise generation with modest overhead, applicable to DP-SGD training.

title: Institutionalizing Ai Diplomacy In Africa | Science
abstract: The contemporary landscape of artificial intelligence (AI) diplomacy in Africa is structurally bound to the continent’s history of science, technology, and innovation (STI) engagement. Colonial-era scientific expeditions sought to catalog geological resources and ecological assets to feed the industrial economies of Western countries, establishing a systemic dependency that relegated Africa to the periphery of the global natural resource trade and other strategic mineral markets. This legacy shaped an international order in which technological advancements across North America, Europe, and East Asia frequently occur through the extraction of African resources, without corresponding technology transfer or local capacity building.

conclusion: Calls for institutionalizing AI diplomacy in Africa to overcome historical imbalances and foster local capacity building.

In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of high-energy emission from the center of our Galaxy. This region contains the closest supermassive black hole to us, which offers the best studied galactic nucleus in the Universe, with its quiescent emission and accretion contrasted by flaring activity. title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Understanding vacuum breakdown is crucial for improving the reliability and efficiency of particle accelerators, fusion reactors, and other high-power technologies.
method: The authors synthesize recent experimental and computational studies to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights could help improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Searching for new hadrons and understanding charmonium decays provides insights into QCD, quark confinement, and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments, highlighting recent advances from BESIII.
result: The review summarizes current knowledge of hadron production in charm-meson pair systems and identifies BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: The field continues to advance with high-precision data from BESIII, contributing to our understanding of strong interaction dynamics.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo's planetary radar was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, enabling detailed characterization of many Solar System objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system made significant contributions to planetary science, and its loss is a major setback for the field.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper is a historical review of radio astronomy achievements at the Arecibo Observatory, with no connection to quantum information theory or quantum technologies.
motivation: The paper aims to document Arecibo's legacy in radio astronomy, covering pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
method: It is a colloquium-style review summarizing historical developments and scientific contributions from Arecibo's five decades of operation.
result: The paper highlights Arecibo's major contributions across diverse astrophysical topics, but does not present new research or technical results.
conclusion: Arecibo's upgrades enabled sustained scientific impact, but the paper is purely historical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances made with the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities for studying the upper atmosphere have enabled significant advances in geospace science, but these results are not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The paper reviews incoherent scatter radar technique and presents key findings from Arecibo's suite of instruments in plasma physics, space weather, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
result: The review highlights advances in understanding ionospheric plasma processes, atomic metal layers, and coupling between the ionosphere and magnetosphere.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been a vital tool for geospace research, but the paper does not contribute to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.

authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.

conclusion: Multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star physics and astrophysics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud phenomena under controlled conditions.
result: Convection-cloud chambers provide insights into turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, helping to bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to address the precipitation bottleneck, but further work is needed to fully explain the rapid transition.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae, focusing on detection and parameter estimation.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would provide unique multimessenger insights into the supernova engine and neutron star physics.
method: The authors summarize recent progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discuss detection methods using ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The paper presents the latest modeling and detection strategies for gravitational waves from core collapse supernovae.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from a nearby supernova will enable multimessenger studies of the central engine and neutron star formation.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a potential challenge to the cosmological principle and ΛCDM model, based on radio galaxy and quasar catalogs.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole anisotropy in the large-scale matter distribution with the cosmic microwave background dipole.
method: Analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to assess the compatibility of the matter dipole with the CMB dipole.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, challenging the standard ΛCDM interpretation.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require modifications to the standard model of cosmology.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.

tldr: A review of astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their effects on dark matter halos.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test self-interacting dark matter models using astrophysical observations.
method: Review of theoretical predictions and observational constraints from galaxies to large-scale structures.

conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, with ongoing and upcoming surveys expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions, plasma physics, and diagnostics like neutrinos and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.

conclusion: The review consolidates recent progress in solar fusion physics, providing a benchmark for stellar evolution models.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.

title: Propagation And Collisionless Damping Of Topologically-protected Surface Plasma Waves In Non-uniformly Magnetized Plasma Columns
authors: Roopendra Singh Rajawat And Gennady Shvets
abstract: Recent theoretical studies revealed the existence of topologically-protected surface plasma waves (TSPWs) in uniformly magnetized cold plasma columns. Reflections-free propagation of the TSPWs along arbitrarily-shaped plasma boundaries oriented perpendicularly to the magnetic field was shown to be preserved even when their collisionless damping by localized upper-hybrid resonances was accounted for. Here we extend this theory to the realistic case of three-dimensional magnetic field produced by finite-sized magnetic coils. We demonstrate that when TSPWs are launched in the direction of the decreasing magnetic field, they are collisionlessly absorbed within a highly localized (evanescent) region as they propagate away from the magnetic coil. We show that the resulting wave reflection can be negligible—in clear contrast with wave reflection from the corresponding evanescence regions of unmagnetized non-uniform plasmas.
tldr: This paper studies topologically-protected surface plasma waves in non-uniformly magnetized plasma columns, focusing on wave propagation and collisionless damping.
motivation: To extend the theory of topologically-protected surface plasma waves from uniform to realistic non-uniform magnetic fields, and to understand wave absorption and reflection in such systems.
method: The authors model a three-dimensional magnetic field from finite-sized coils and analyze wave propagation and damping using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They find that waves launched in the direction of decreasing magnetic field are collisionlessly absorbed in a localized evanescent region, with negligible reflection, contrasting with unmagnetized plasmas.
conclusion: The study demonstrates robust unidirectional propagation and absorption of TSPWs in non-uniform magnetized plasmas, which may have implications for plasma heating and wave control.

title: Search For Decays Of The Higgs Boson Into Pair-produced Pseudoscalar Particles Decaying Into Τ + ...

abstract: A search for a pair of low-mass pseudoscalars that promptly decay into -leptons is presented using 140 fb of proton–proton collision data at TeV centre-of-mass energy recorded with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. The result is used to place constraints on exotic decays of the Higgs boson into four -leptons, . This search focuses on events with either one or two -leptons decaying into hadrons and neutrinos, and the remaining three or two -leptons decaying into either electron or muon and neutrinos. No significant excess is observed above the expected Standard Model background and upper limits at the 95% confidence level on are set ranging from 0.06 to 0.23, depending on the mass ranging from 15 to 60 GeV.
tldr: This paper reports an ATLAS search for exotic Higgs decays to pseudoscalars decaying to tau leptons, with no significant excess over the Standard Model.
motivation: To probe beyond-Standard-Model physics via Higgs boson decays to light pseudoscalars, motivated by models like the next-to-minimal supersymmetric standard model.
method: Analyzes 140 fb^-1 of 13 TeV pp collision data from ATLAS, selecting events with hadronic and leptonic tau decays, and performing a statistical analysis to set limits.
result: No significant excess observed; 95% CL upper limits on the branching ratio are set between 0.06 and 0.23 for pseudoscalar masses 15–60 GeV.
conclusion: The results constrain exotic Higgs decays, but do not show evidence for new physics.

title: Defect Approach To Giant Graviton Dynamics
authors: Yunfeng Jiang And Xinan Zhou Junding Chen
abstract: We develop a framework of zero dimensional defects for analyzing light–light–heavy–heavy (LLHH) correlators in conformal field theories. We specifically apply this formalism to correlators of giant gravitons in super Yang–Mills to probe the nontrivial physics beyond planarity. By combining this framework with bootstrap techniques, we compute all four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons of arbitrary dimensions. We identify a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry—a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry–present at both strong and weak coupling, which allows these correlators to be packaged into a single generating function. Furthermore, we perform a systematic OPE analysis of the strong-coupling correlators, extracting the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for the defect-channel double-particle operators. Finally, we argue that the defect perspective provides the natural nonperturbative description for any LLHH correlator by showing that four-point conformal blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.
tldr: This paper develops a defect framework for analyzing LLHH correlators in conformal field theories, applied to giant gravitons in super Yang-Mills theory.
motivation: To understand non-planar corrections in AdS/CFT by studying correlators involving heavy operators like giant gravitons.
method: Combines zero-dimensional defect formalism with bootstrap techniques to compute four-point functions at strong coupling.
result: Identifies a hidden 10d conformal symmetry and extracts the full spectrum of anomalous dimensions for defect-channel operators.
conclusion: The defect perspective provides a natural nonperturbative description for LLHH correlators in the heavy limit.

title: Orthogonal Phase Modulation And Lissajous Mode Decoupling In Light-induced Thermoelastic Spectroscopy For Real-time Multi-component Gas Sensing
authors: Hanxu Ma, Shunda Qiao, Ying He, Haiyue Sun And Yufei Ma
abstract: This paper proposed an optical detection mechanism that utilized orthogonal phase modulation (OPM) and Lissajous mode decoupling within a light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy (LITES) sensor for the first time, enabling real-time multi-component gas sensing. By establishing a two-dimensional forced vibration model of a quartz tuning fork (QTF) under dual-path OPM, it revealed the vibration mode coupling mechanism induced by non-ideal phase and amplitude conditions, thereby providing a theoretical basis and optimization pathway for suppressing channel crosstalk. In the OPM-LITES sensor, two continuous-wave distributed feedback lasers were modulated by sinusoidal waves with the same frequency (f0/2, where f0 is the resonant frequency of the QTF) but a phase difference of 45°. The combined beam, after wavelength division multiplexing, co-excited the self-designed low-frequency QTF. The piezoelectric signal generated by the QTF underwent orthogonal demodulation via a lock-in amplifier (LIA). The concentration information for the two gases was independently retrieved from the decoupled X-component and Y-component of the LIA. Experimental results demonstrated that the OPM-LITES sensor exhibited excellent linear responses to both methane (CH4) and acetylene (C2H2), with average relative systematic errors of 0.54% and 0.79%, and maximum relative errors of 1.72% and 1.38%, respectively. Allan deviation analysis indicated that the minimum detection limits (MDLs) for CH4 and C2H2 reached 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, with normalized noise-equivalent absorption coefficients of 5.09 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2 and 6.18 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2, respectively. This study not only provided a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection but also established a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling and signal processing in spectroscopic sensing.
tldr: This paper presents a novel optical gas sensing technique using orthogonal phase modulation and Lissajous mode decoupling in light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy for real-time multi-component gas detection.
motivation: Real-time multi-component gas sensing is important for environmental monitoring and industrial safety, but existing methods suffer from channel crosstalk and complexity.
method: The authors use two continuous-wave lasers modulated at the same frequency with a 45° phase difference, co-exciting a quartz tuning fork. The piezoelectric signal is orthogonally demodulated to decouple the gas concentration information.
result: The sensor achieves linear responses for methane and acetylene with low systematic errors (0.54% and 0.79%) and detection limits of 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, respectively.
conclusion: The proposed OPM-LITES sensor provides a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection with a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling.

SignificanceAntibodies are highly selective therapeutics, but their clinical utility has been limited to extracellular targets due to their membrane impermeability. Many disease-relevant proteins, including transcription factors, oncoproteins, and ...
tldr: This paper presents a method for intracellular delivery of full-length antibodies using organ-targeted lipid nanoparticles.
motivation: Antibodies are highly selective therapeutics but cannot cross cell membranes, limiting their use to extracellular targets. Many disease-relevant proteins are intracellular, so a delivery method is needed.
method: The authors developed lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) functionalized with targeting ligands to deliver full-length antibodies into specific cell types in vivo.
result: The LNPs successfully delivered functional antibodies into target cells in animal models, enabling intracellular targeting of proteins such as transcription factors.
conclusion: Organ-targeted LNPs provide a viable platform for intracellular antibody delivery, expanding the therapeutic potential of antibodies to intracellular targets.

SignificanceCa2+signaling in mammalian endothelial cells (ECs) regulates blood flow, force-sensing, and vessel permeability. While past studies have investigated EC Ca2+signaling in 2D monolayers and the 3D mouse brain, how Ca2+signaling is organized ...
tldr: This paper studies Ca2+ signaling in skin capillary endothelial cells, a topic in cell biology and physiology.
motivation: To understand how Ca2+ signaling is organized in skin capillary endothelial cells, which is important for blood flow regulation and vessel permeability.
method: Experimental imaging and analysis of Ca2+ activity in endothelial cells in vivo or in vitro.
result: The study finds that skin capillary endothelial cells form a network of spatiotemporally conserved Ca2+ activity.
conclusion: The organization of Ca2+ signaling in skin capillaries may have implications for vascular function and disease.
